stem:
Acidified potassium dichromate(VI) can oxidise ethanedioic acid, $\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$. The relevant half-equations are shown.

$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

$$\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^-$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the overall equation for the reaction between acidified dichromate(VI) ions and ethanedioic acid.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In an experiment a $0.242\text{ g}$ sample of hydrated ethanedioic acid, $\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4.\boldsymbol{x}\text{H}_2\text{O}$, was reacted with a $0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of acidified potassium dichromate(VI).

$32.0\text{ cm}^3$ of the acidified potassium dichromate(VI) solution was required for complete oxidation of the ethanedioic acid.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of dichromate(VI) ions used to react with the sample of ethanedioic acid.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of ethanedioic acid in the sample.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass, $M_r$, of the hydrated ethanedioic acid.
